set_up.summary: This project can be run using Docker Compose for isolated environments, Makefile for local development, or manual setup, with Docker Compose being the most reliable method.

env_vars.name: ENVIRONMENT
env_vars.purpose: Determines application behavior (DEVELOPMENT, STAGING, PRODUCTION); used in entrypoint.sh to set LOG_LEVEL and other configurations.

env_vars.name: REDIS_PORT
env_vars.purpose: Overrides the default Redis port (6379) when running locally or in staging; used in docker-compose files to map container port.

env_vars.name: POSTGRES_USER
env_vars.purpose: Database username for PostgreSQL; set in docker-compose files and loaded via .env to authenticate connections.

env_vars.name: POSTGRES_PASSWORD
env_vars.purpose: Database password for PostgreSQL; set in docker-compose files and loaded via .env to authenticate connections.

env_vars.name: POSTGRES_DB
env_vars.purpose: Database name for PostgreSQL; set in docker-compose files and loaded via .env to determine the default database to connect to.

env_vars.name: PORT
env_vars.purpose: Overrides the default API port (8000); used in entrypoint.sh to configure Uvicorn or Gunicorn binds.

env_vars.name: HOST
env_vars.purpose: Overrides the default bind host (0.0.0.0); used in entrypoint.sh to configure Uvicorn or Gunicorn binds.

env_vars.name: WORKERS
env_vars.purpose: Overrides the number of Gunicorn workers; used in entrypoint.sh and gunicorn.conf.py for production tuning.

env_vars.name: LOG_LEVEL
env_vars.purpose: Explicitly sets the application log level; if unset, defaults based on ENVIRONMENT in entrypoint.sh and gunicorn.conf.py.

files_guide.purpose: Production-grade Docker Compose configuration; uses production build target, no volume mounts, and runs Gunicorn with Uvicorn workers.
Development-focused configuration for the 'stitchsense' project; uses development Dockerfile with hot reload via volume mounts and uvicorn --reload.
Local development setup for the 'ramp' project; similar to dev but uses a single context root, mounts entire source tree, and targets development stage.
Staging environment configuration; uses development build target but expects environment variables from .env and is aligned with production-like settings.
Multi-stage Dockerfile for the API service; defines base, dependencies, development (for uvicorn reload), and production stages with proper user and file permissions.
Dockerfile for Celery workers; builds a minimal Python image with Celery, Redis, AWS SDK, and installs dependencies from poetry.lock without the root package.
Configuration for Gunicorn to serve the FastAPI application in production; sets workers, logging, Uvicorn worker class, and lifecycle hooks.
Core Nginx configuration for the entire stack; defines general HTTP settings, gzip, security headers, and includes conf.d/*.conf for route-specific rules.
Nginx reverse proxy configuration; routes traffic from public domains (api.stitchsense.ai) to api-main:8000 and handles SSL termination.
Configuration for Alembic database migration tool; points to migrations directory and enables script path resolution relative to the project root.
Task runner for local development; abstracts common Python, Alembic, and testing commands using Poetry to manage dependencies.
Verification script to ensure required tools (Docker, Python 3.11+, AWS CLI, Node.js via nvm) are installed and configured on the host system.
Entrypoint script for both development and production containers; loads .env variables, normalizes ENVIRONMENT, sets defaults, and validates Python packages before starting the server.

The core logic resides in the 'src' module, which is depended upon by migrations, tests, and the root configuration, while infrastructure components like Docker, Nginx, and Terraform handle deployment.

Race conditions during token upsert could result in duplicate or inconsistent user-auth state.
Unhandled GitHub API rate limits or errors may break the flow without proper user feedback.

flows.name: Repository Scanning
flows.description: Scans connected GitHub repositories for code structure, dependencies, and function calls to build static analysis data.
risks: GitHub API rate limits may interrupt scanning if not handled with retries or pagination.
Large repositories may cause memory exhaustion during tree traversal or file parsing.
Incomplete or malformed source files could lead to parser failures or incomplete call graphs.
Database write conflicts may occur if concurrent scans attempt to replace repository data.
Missing or invalid GitHub OAuth tokens can result in failed repository access.
